BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r3.claim: The mockers ask when God will establish the Hour; ayyan means “when,” and mursa is the fixing or establishing of its time.
BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r3.anchor: إرساؤها أي إقامتها يريدون متى يقيمها الله ويثبتها

BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r4.claim: Because a time cannot directly predicate an event, the grammatical estimate is “at what time is its appointed establishment”; the questioners mockingly invoke the Hour’s terrifying descriptions.
BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r4.anchor: فأيان ظرف بمعنى متى وأصله أي آن ووقت والمرسي مصدر بمعنى الإرساء

QASHANI:79:34-41/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:34-41/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:34-41/r6.claim: Knowledge of the Hour ends with God: knowing it requires the annihilation of one’s knowledge in divine knowledge and one’s self in God’s Self.
QASHANI:79:34-41/r6.anchor: فكيف يعلمها ولا علم له ولا ذات، فمن أين أنت وغيرك من علمها

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4.claim: The Prophet should not be troubled by demands for the Hour’s timing: only God knows it, the Prophet’s duty is warning, and at its sight people will feel they stayed only a short while.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4.anchor: The time of arrival of the Day of Judgement is something which only the Almighty knows

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p167/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p167/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p167/r3.claim: The Prophet is assured that the questioners tease him about when Judgment will arrive, while his responsibility is to warn and give the heedful a chance to prepare.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p167/r3.anchor: the only responsibility of the Prophet (sws) was to inform people

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p167/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p167/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p167/r4.claim: The word ayān asks when a future event occurs, not where; marṣāhā's port and anchoring image makes the question sarcastic.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p167/r4.anchor: it would be erroneous to translate it as “where;”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r2.claim: Quraysh repeatedly asked when the Hour would happen because the Prophet warned them of it; the verse came in response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r2.anchor: وكانوا يلحون في البحث عن وقت الساعة، إذ كان يتوعدهم بها ويكثر من ذلك، فنزلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r3.claim: أيان مرساها asks when the Hour is established; alternatively it asks its end or resting place, like a ship's anchorage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r3.anchor: أيان مرساها: متى إقامتها؟ أي متى يقيهما الله ويثبتها ويكونها؟

FARRA:v3p234/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p234/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p234/r1.claim: The Hour's mooring is compared to a ship that stops: its standing means that it appears and is established, like justice or truth standing.
FARRA:v3p234/r1.anchor: هي بمنزلة السفينة إذا كانت جارية فرست، ورسوها قيامها،

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p513#8/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p513#8/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p513#8/r1.claim: Ayyān marsāhā asks when the Hour will arrive and settle; its signs precede it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p513#8/r1.anchor: {أيان مرساها} أي متى تأتي فتستقر؟ لأن الأشراط تتقدمها.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p37/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37/r1.claim: They ask when the Hour will be established; مرساها is a time noun from rasa, meaning becoming fixed or firm, as with firmly rooted mountains.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37/r1.anchor: أي متى إرساؤها أي إقامتها يريدون متى يقيمها الله تعالى ويكونها ويثبتها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p37/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37/r2.claim: Another gloss makes مرساها its endpoint or place of settlement, as for a ship; the author notes the mismatch between a question about when and a place comparison, then proposes a metaphor of the distant day as a traveler.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37/r2.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المرسى بمعنى المنتهى أي متى منتهاها ومستقرها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r7.claim: The question about the Hour asks when it will appear and be established.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r7.anchor: متى ظهورها وثبوتها. {فيم أنت من ذكراها} لست في شيء من علمها وذكرها

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r2.claim: مرساها asks when the Hour is established, or where it ends and settles, like a ship’s mooring.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r2.anchor: { يسئلونك عن الساعة أيان مرسها } متى إرساؤها أي إقامتها وإثباتها

BINTSHATI:v1p159/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r1.claim: The Qur’an’s warning has reached its culmination, then it settles the question of the Hour by saying its final knowledge belongs to God.
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r1.anchor: لا يدع الموقف دون أن يعقب عليه بحسم عقدته، والرد على سؤالهم عن الساعة

BINTSHATI:v1p159/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r2.claim: In Arabic, sāʿah first denotes a portion of time, later conventionally specified as sixty minutes; the Qur’anic eschatological usage is distinctive.
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r2.anchor: ولفظ الساعة في العربية، يعني الجزء من الوقت، ثم تحدد. بستين دقيقة

BINTSHATI:v1p159/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r3.claim: When indefinite, sāʿah in the Qur’an denotes a short, unspecified span, while the definite Hour consistently means the Afterlife’s decisive event.
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r3.anchor: أما حين يستعمل القرآن "الساعة" معرفة بـ: ال، فتلك - دائماً - هي ساعة الآخرة

BINTSHATI:v1p159/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r4.claim: The Hour is presented as active and momentous through verbs of coming and rising, marking the change in cosmic order.
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r4.anchor: أن هذه "الساعة" تنفرد دون ساعات الزمان كله، بأنها الحاسمة الفاصلة التي يتغير فيها نظام الزمن

BINTSHATI:v1p159/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r5.claim: In ordinary Arabic, the definite sāʿah can mean the present moment; later the word also named the timekeeping instrument.
BINTSHATI:v1p159/r5.anchor: ويستعمل معرفا بـ (ال) للعهد، ظرف زمان للوقت الحاضر، فيقال: أزورك الساعة

NAHHAS:v5p146/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r11.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p146/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ asks why the Hour uses irsāʾ, normally for ships and mountains; the answer compares it to a ship that runs then moors, meaning the Hour becomes established and manifest.
NAHHAS:v5p146/r11.anchor: قال الفراء يقال إنما الإرساء للسفينة والجبال وما أشبههن فكيف وصفت الساعة بالإرساء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r2.claim: The name al-Nāziʿāt points to angels extracting souls and then the account of Pharaoh and Moses; al-Sāhirah and al-Ṭāmmah also fit the oath and the surah’s flow.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r2.anchor: وصور ذلك بنزع الأرواح بأيدي الملائكة الكرام ، ثم أمر فرعون اللعين وموسى عليه السلام ، واسمها النازعات واضح في ذلك المرام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r1.claim: Quraysh repeatedly ask mockingly when the Resurrection will occur, with marsā meaning its setting, occurrence, or establishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r1.anchor: أي قريش على سبيل التجديد والاستمرار سؤال استهزاء وإنكار واستبعاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r5.claim: The question about the Hour begins an explanatory resumption prompted by the disbelievers' repeated, mocking questions about its timing and their demand that it be hastened.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r5.anchor: استئناف بياني منشؤه أن المشركين كانوا يسألون عن وقت حلول الساعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r6.claim: They imagine the delay disproves the Hour, reasoning that an angry God would immediately retaliate like an impetuous human; the Quran rejects this human analogy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r6.anchor: وكان سؤالهم استهزاء واستخفافا لأنهم عقدوا قلوبهم على استحالة وقوع الساعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r1.claim: After proving resurrection and describing its punishment, the passage answers the question about when the Great Calamity will arrive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r1.anchor: لما قضي حق الاستدلال على إمكان البعث بإقامة الدليل وضرب الأمثال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r2.claim: The questioners are the disbelievers who earlier asked whether they would be restored to their former state.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r2.anchor: فضمير ( يسألون ) عائد إلى المشركين أصحاب القلوب الواجفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r3.claim: The imperfect verb presents their question as recurring and repeated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r3.anchor: وحكي فعل السؤال بصيغة المضارع للدلالة على تجدد هذا السؤال وتكرره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r4.claim: Calling the Hour ‘the Hour’ rather than repeating ‘the Great Calamity’ gives the sentence independent force and varies the naming.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r4.anchor: والساعة : هي الطامة فذكر الساعة إظهار في مقام الإضمار لقصد استقلال الجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r5.claim: Ayyan asks for a specific time; the question implies that the event is remote or even impossible, while marsa is a ship's mooring metaphor for the Hour's arrival.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p94/r5.anchor: والاستفهام مستعمل في الاستبعاد كناية وهو أيضا كناية عن الاستحالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r4.claim: The reply addresses the apparent request for timing and their use of delay to deny the Hour: it will occur, and the waiting will seem no longer than part of a day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r4.anchor: فأجيبوا على طريقة الأسلوب الحكيم ، أي إن طال تأخر حصولها فإنها واقعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r9.claim: Quraysh repeatedly pressed the Prophet about the Hour's timing, which occasioned this verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r9.anchor: وقوله تعالى: يسئلونك عن الساعة الآية نزلت بسبب أن قريشا كانت تلح في البعث عن وقت الساعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r10.claim: أيان مرساها means when it will be established or anchored, like a ship reaching its mooring.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r10.anchor: و: أيان مرساها معناه: متى ثبوتها ووقت رسوها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r11.speaker: الأعرج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r11.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads إيان with kasra on its initial alif.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي: «إيان» بكسر الألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r13.speaker: عائشة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r13.claim: Aisha says the Prophet was often asked about the Hour but stopped after this verse was revealed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r13.anchor: وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يسأل عن الساعة كثيرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#8/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#8/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#8/r1.claim: The question about when the Hour will occur was explained at al-Aʿrāf 7:187.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r7.claim: Only God knows the appointed time of the Hour; its knowledge is beyond the Prophet and all creation, as another verse says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r7.anchor: أي: ليس علمها إليك ولا إلى أحد من الخلق، بل مردها ومرجعها إلى الله عز وجل،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r8.claim: When Gabriel asked the Prophet when the Hour would come, he replied that the one asked knew no more than the asker.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r8.anchor: جبريل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن وقت الساعة قال: "ما المسئول عنها بأعلم من السائل".

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r8.claim: Ayyān means “when” and is commonly used to ask about time, as ayn asks about place.
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r8.anchor: و(أيان) معناه: متى، وكثر استعماله في السؤال عن الزمان

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r9.claim: Marsā can mean the ship's becoming fixed, the source noun for anchoring, or the time of anchoring.
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r9.anchor: والمرسى: قيامها ثابتة، ويحتمل أن يكون المراد به المرسى المصدر

JISHUMI:v10p7277/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r4.claim: The time of the Resurrection is known only to God.
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r4.anchor: ومنها: أن وقت القيامة لا يعلمه غير الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r1.claim: أيان مرساها asks when the Hour will be established and brought into being; alternatively it asks for its end or resting place, like a ship's anchorage.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r1.anchor: متى إرساؤها ، أي إقامتها ، أرادوا : متى يقيمها الله ويثبتها ويكونها ؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p700/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p700/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p700/r1.claim: A report promises that whoever recites Surat al-Nazi'at will be held in the grave and at the Resurrection only as long as an obligatory prayer, then enter Paradise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p700/r1.anchor: من قرأ سورة والنازعات كان ممن حبسه الله في القبر والقيامة حتى يدخل الجنة قدر صلاة المكتوبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r10.claim: أيان مرساها asks when the Hour will occur.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس : متى زمانها , قاله الربيع

MUQATIL:79:42-46/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:42-46/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:42-46/r1.claim: When Quraysh ask when the Hour will arrive, God answers that no one in the heavens or earth knows the unseen except God, as stated in 27:65.
MUQATIL:79:42-46/r1.anchor: { يسألونك } يعني كفار مكة { عن الساعة أيان مرساها } [آية: 42]

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#3/r1.claim: They ask when the Hour will be established, meaning when God will set it in place.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#3/r1.anchor: متى ارساؤها أى اقامتها يعنى متى يقيمها الله تعالى ويثبتها

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r1.claim: The Meccan polytheists asked the Prophet mockingly when the Hour would occur, prompting the revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r1.anchor: سأل مشركو مكة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم متى تكون الساعة استهزاء

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r3.claim: Mursāhā means its establishment or occurrence; the root evokes a ship coming to rest.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r4.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r4.claim: The Hour's coming to rest is like a ship settling at anchor.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r5.claim: Mursāhā means its endpoint, as a ship's anchorage is where it ends its course.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: أي منتهاها، ومرسى السفينة حيث تنتهي.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r6.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r6.claim: Mursāhā asks when the Hour's time will be.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r7.claim: These explanations are close in meaning; the subject was discussed earlier in al-A'raf.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r7.anchor: والمعنى متقارب. وقد مضى في «الأعراف» بيان ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r8.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r8.claim: A Prophetic report says the Hour will occur only with an anger that God becomes angry.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r8.anchor: لا تقوم الساعة إلا بغضبة يغضبها ربك

ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r4.claim: Ayyāna means “when,” asking the time of the Hour’s occurrence and arising.

RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r1.claim: After proving Resurrection possible, affirming it, and describing its general and moral states, the passage turns to the question of its timing.
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r1.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما بين بالبرهان العقلي إمكان القيامة ، ثم أخبر عن وقوعها

RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r2.claim: The polytheists may ask sarcastically to make followers think Resurrection baseless, or impatiently demand its time, as in 42:18.
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r2.anchor: فقالوا على سبيل الاستهزاء : { أيان مرساها }

RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r3.claim: Mursa may mean when God establishes and brings the Hour into being, or its endpoint and resting place, like a ship's mooring.

RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r4.claim: One reading asks why the Prophet is occupied with remembering and disclosing its appointed time; Aisha reports that he kept mentioning and being asked about the Hour until this verse came down.
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r4.anchor: وعن عائشة ( لم يزل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يذكر الساعة ويسأل عنها

RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r5.claim: Another reading rebukes the question itself: the Prophet, final messenger, has given signs of the Hour's nearness, enough to prepare people, while its knowledge belongs to God alone.
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r5.anchor: أرسلك وأنت خاتم الأنبياء وآخر الرسل ذاكرا من أنواع علاماتها

STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10.claim: The final verses answer disbelievers who taunted the Prophet for not knowing when the Hour would arrive.
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10.anchor: respond to the disbelievers who chided the Prophet for not knowing when the Hour would come

STUDYQURAN:79:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:42/r1.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:42/r1.claim: The question is attributed to Makkan idolaters who asked to mock, not to gain information.
STUDYQURAN:79:42/r1.anchor: the idolaters of Makkah, who did not ask in order to be informed, but only to mock

STUDYQURAN:79:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:42/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:42/r2.claim: The wording derives from a nautical metaphor, asking when the Hour will berth.
STUDYQURAN:79:42/r2.anchor: derives from a nautical metaphor meaning, “When shall it berth?”

STUDYQURAN:79:42/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:42/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:42/r3.claim: Some take the nautical image to imply that the Hour is near.
STUDYQURAN:79:42/r3.anchor: Some take the use of this metaphor to imply that it is near at hand

TAB-FULL:v24p100/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r1.claim: The deniers ask when the Resurrection will be established and appear; irsāʾ is like a ship coming to rest, meaning that the Hour's advent becomes manifest and fixed, like justice or truth standing.
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r1.anchor: رسوها: قيامها؛ قال: وليس قيامها كقيام القائم، إنما هي كقولك: قد قام العدل، وقام الحق

TAB-FULL:v24p100/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r4.speaker: طارق بن شهاب
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r4.claim: Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb says the Prophet continually mentioned the Hour until the warning passage was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r4.anchor: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يزال يذكر شأن الساعة حتى نزلت

TABATABAI:79:42-44/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r1.claim: The passage answers repeated questions about the Hour by saying only God knows when it will come.
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r1.anchor: تعرض لسؤالهم عن وقت قيام الساعة ورد له بأن علمه ليس لأحد إلا الله فقد خصه بنفسه

TABATABAI:79:42-44/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r2.claim: The imperfect “they ask” suggests ongoing questioning: after hearing about resurrection, the mockers repeatedly demanded a date; marsā is a verbal noun meaning establishment or settling.
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r2.anchor: الظاهر أن التعبير بيسألونك لإفادة الاستمرار فقد كان المشركون بعد ما سمعوا حديث القيامة

TABATABAI:79:46#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r3.claim: The Qummi commentary glosses the question as “when does it come?” and says its knowledge belongs to God.
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r3.anchor: قال متى تقوم؟ فقال الله { إلى ربك منتهاها } أي علمها عند الله

TABATABAI:79:46#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r5.claim: A weak-chain report says Meccan polytheists mockingly asked the Prophet when the Hour would come, and these verses were revealed.
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r5.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن ابن عباس قال إن مشركي مكة سألوا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقالوا متى تقوم الساعة استهزاء منهم

TABATABAI:79:46#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r7.speaker: عائشة
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet answered Bedouins by pointing to the youngest person and saying their Hour would come if he lived a century; the author rejects this as an unsuitable date-setting, since revelation repeatedly says only God knows the Hour.
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r7.anchor: كانت الأعراب إذا قدموا على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سألوه عن الساعة فينظر إلى أحدث إنسان فيهم

TABRISI:79:45-46/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:45-46/r9.claim: The question about when the Hour will be established asks when it will occur as described.
TABRISI:79:45-46/r9.anchor: أي متى يكون قيامها ثابتة على ما وصفتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202/r1.claim: The question means when the Hour will occur and be established; its explanation is at the end of Surat al-Aʿraf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202/r1.anchor: مفسر في آخر سورة الأعراف (¬3) (¬4) -أي متى وقوعها، وقيامها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r1.claim: The question asks when the Resurrection will occur and be established.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r1.anchor: { يسألونك عن الساعة } يعني: القيامة. { أيان مرساها } متى وقوعها وثبوتها؟

ELMALILI:79:42-46/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r1.claim: Mursa is a verbal noun of bringing something to rest, or a place or time meaning endpoint; like a ship anchored, the question asks when God will bring the Hour to pass.
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r1.anchor: Burada bir istiare var demek olur. Yani Allah o Sâ‘at’i ne vakit getirip dikecek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r1.claim: Disbelieving polytheists repeatedly asked the Prophet when Resurrection would occur to put him in difficulty, sometimes mockingly wishing it would come soon because they deemed it impossible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r1.anchor: Müşrikler kıyamet ve âhirete inanmadıkları için her fırsatta Hz. Peygamber’e kıyametin ne zaman kopacağını sorarak onu zor duruma düşürmeye çalışıyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r2.claim: The Prophet wished he could answer, hoping a response might help them believe.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r2.anchor: Hz. Peygamber ise onların iman etmelerine vesile olur ümidiyle, “Keşke sorularına cevap vermek mümkün olsaydı!” diye temennide bulunuyordu

BURHAN:v3p451/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p451/r2.speaker: ابن أبي الحديد
BURHAN:v3p451/r2.claim: Ibn Abī al-Ḥadīd denies jinās between the two uses of الساعة: they have one meaning, whereas jinās requires distinct real meanings; making one figurative also defeats the category.
BURHAN:v3p451/r2.anchor: الأول نازع ابن أبي الحديد في الآية الأولى وقال عندي 3 أنه ليس بتجنيس أصلا وأن الساعة في الموضعين بمعنى واحد
